scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W007 anchor image confirms: the mouth is large and red-rimmed with white tooth blocks, but the form is a head with visible eye zones and crossing lines — describing it as a 'circular form' is accurate but the observation that 'lines press outward from the mouth as their source' overstates; the mouth is prominent but the eye zones and spiral are co-equal features. WhyHere corrected to avoid overclaiming the mouth as sole anchor.

W053: observations confirm wide dark void between two tooth rows and three eye-like forms overhead — role as 'mouth as anchor' is visually supported. Transition from W007 is valid: W007 has a containing circular outline; W053's mouth breaks past any single boundary.

W168: the jaw-like form does fill the canvas and tooth row is prominent, but two circular eye zones are clearly visible and substantial — describing them as 'secondary marks' understates them. WhyHere softened.
W048: two stacked jaw forms are visible. Transition from W168 (one jaw to two) is visually supported.
W044: marquee border of repeating ovals and rectangles is confirmed visible. Transition from W048 is valid.
W069: coral/orange field and spiked crown confirmed. Transition from W044 (geometric border vs organic zigzags) is valid.
W121: zigzag marks appear in eye zones as well as mouth — confirmed. Transition from W069 is valid.

W157 anchor image confirms: nested rectangular loops around both eye zones and mouth, tooth row with dark gap, yellow vertical stripe left, yellow bar right. The draft's whyHere mentions 'nested concentric loops' which is accurate. The final sentence about 'the collector sees the nested loops as kin to scrimshaw' is inappropriate — this is visitor prose and must not reference the collector or scrimshaw comparison. Removed.

W287 anchor image confirms: two rectangular eye zones with yellow cross-hatching, spiky crown forms above each eye, countable tooth row with red-outlined lips, blue dominant field, diagonal forehead stripes, stacked orange/red forms at right edge. The description is accurate. Transition from W157 (black ground inward loops to blue field exposed frontality) is visually supported.

W059: amber field confirmed, red spiral at eye confirmed, open mouth with teeth confirmed. Transition from W287 (blue field advancing vs amber holding at distance) is a ground-color contrast that is visually supported.
W078: acid-yellow ground with overlapping translucent circles confirmed, open jaw with teeth confirmed. Transition from W059 is valid.
W228: flat bright blue field confirmed, heart and flower eye shapes confirmed, alternating black-and-white tooth row confirmed. Transition from W078 is valid.
W262: saturated yellow field confirmed, two red heart eye zones confirmed, tooth row confirmed. Transition from W228 (blue holds at distance, yellow advances) is visually supported.
W073: ochre/teal washes under black loops confirmed, red-edged mouth with narrow tooth row confirmed. Transition from W262 is valid.

W277: teal-green field confirmed, heavy circular form with warm interior confirmed, spiked jaw with white zigzag verticals confirmed. Transition from W073 (warm throughout vs warm/cool split) is visually supported.
W115: two face-like forms on black field confirmed — ringed eye left, open-mouthed form right. Transition from W277 (single form to two forms) is valid.
W229: white-outlined oval with two tooth-lined shapes and red-orange bar confirmed. Transition from W115 is valid.

W259: observations are thin — only three bullet points, one of which ('broad warm-colored bands pass across the face') is vague. The image shows a tilted head with yellow circular eye forms and multiple tooth rows. WhyHere and transition are acceptable given limited observation data; a limitation note is added.
W253: circular form with outward-pulling lines and white verticals in open lower section confirmed. Transition from W259 is valid.
W015: yellow disc with grinning face, crossed bars with teeth, heavy red field below confirmed. Transition from W253 (both circular, but pressure direction differs) is visually supported.
W182: swollen olive-green face filling frame, crossed scribbles, bared teeth confirmed. Transition from W015 (disc floating vs face filling frame) is valid.
W232: two mismatched eyes (one gridded, one with red X), drips from top, open-toothed mouth, gray background confirmed. Transition from W182 (symmetrical density vs deliberate asymmetry) is valid.
W268: dark layered interior, goggle shapes, bared tooth row, bright escaping lines on black field confirmed. Transition from W232 (gray ground vs black field) is valid.
W157 whyHere: removed unsupported collector/scrimshaw reference from visitor prose.
W259 observations are notably sparse compared to other works; the whyHere and transition are kept but flagged as relying on limited evidence.
Chapter 'The Mouth as Anchor' title and framing: W168 eye zones are substantial, not merely secondary — whyHere adjusted to reflect this without abandoning the chapter's logic.
No invented objects, no unsupported artist psychology, no chronology or influence claims found after corrections.
Pacing: opening (anchor) → decorated field → ground effects → doubled forms → surface pressure provides a clear arc with contrast and conclusion. Confirmed adequate.
W015 is placed in the final chapter rather than earlier; its disc form creates a valid echo with W253 that opens that chapter well.

evidence.limitation: Ensemble sheet review and three original anchors; not full-resolution individual inspection of every work or a visitor study
evidence.wordingReviewScope: Text-only tightening of image-reviewed headings and invitations; no new image inspection or membership change

title: The Shape of a Mouth
question: How do similar teeth leave an expression unresolved?
introduction: Compare the shape of a mouth with its teeth, surrounding lines and colored ground. Individual teeth may remain distinct or join a larger band of marks. Follow changes in spacing, framing and jaw shape across different heads. A possible grin or grimace remains a reading to test against the rest of the drawing.
closing: Find two mouths with similar teeth. Which surrounding features change the way you read their expressions?

chapters.title: The Mouth as Structural Center
chapters.introduction: Four works where the open mouth is the feature that draws the eye first and organizes everything else around it — other marks read as secondary to that central gap.

stops.whyHere: A large red-rimmed tooth row dominates the lower face; white block teeth set against a dark gap compete with the spiral eye and crossing lines for first attention.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #200

stops.whyHere: Three uneven eye-forms overhead, but the wide dark void between two tooth rows pulls the eye downward and holds it; the body mass and scribbled lines radiate outward from that opening.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #200's mouth sits inside a circular head outline; here the mouth breaks past any single containing boundary, becoming the widest opening in the frame.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #57

stops.whyHere: A jaw-like form fills the entire canvas; the tooth row runs across the lower third while two circular eye zones above it read as secondary to the dominant open jaw.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #57 surrounds its mouth with a heavy body mass; nnxyz nnotb #202 strips that body away almost entirely, leaving the jaw and tooth row as the composition's primary event.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #202

stops.whyHere: Two stacked jaw forms — one crowned by a spiral eye, one packed with rounded tooth shapes — double the mouth motif; the composition is built from layered jaw shapes rather than a single face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #202 gives one jaw the whole canvas; nnxyz nnotb #206 stacks two jaw forms vertically, making the repetition of the jaw shape itself the subject.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #206

chapters.title: Teeth Inside a Decorated Field
chapters.introduction: Five works where the mouth competes with dense borders, zigzag lines, and repeating ornamental marks — the tooth row present but carrying equal visual weight with its surroundings.

stops.whyHere: A marquee-like border of repeating ovals and rectangles frames the bared mouth and bulging eyes; the decoration and the teeth carry equal visual weight across the composition.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #206's jaws push outward against a loose field; nnxyz nnotb #67 locks its mouth inside a tight geometric border that holds everything at the same pitch.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #67

stops.whyHere: A hot coral field and spiked crown of orange-yellow ovals compete with the white tooth row; the mouth is one loud element among several rather than the sole focus.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #67's border is geometric and regular; nnxyz nnotb #211 replaces it with organic zigzags and radiating spikes that press against the mouth from all sides.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #211

stops.whyHere: Zigzag tooth-like marks appear inside the rectangular eye zones as well as the mouth, spreading the tooth motif across the whole face structure simultaneously.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #211's decoration stays outside the face features; nnxyz nnotb #269 folds the zigzag mark into the eye zones themselves, so teeth appear in multiple registers at once.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #269

stops.whyHere: Nested rectangular loops surround both the mouth and the eye zones; the tooth row sits inside layered red and orange rings that echo the concentric framing above it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #269 uses zigzag lines throughout; nnxyz nnotb #256 replaces the zigzag with concentric rectangular loops, giving the same density a more compressed, inward pull.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #256

stops.whyHere: Spiky crown forms above each rectangular eye zone and a countable tooth row below distribute the decorative and the dental evenly across the whole face on an open blue field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #256's loops press inward on a black ground; nnxyz nnotb #274 opens onto a blue field where the same density of marks feels more exposed and frontal.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #274

chapters.title: Grounds That Change the Reading
chapters.introduction: Six works where the background color — amber, yellow, blue, ochre-teal, or teal-green — alters how the mouth and teeth register against it, shifting the same tooth form each time.

stops.whyHere: A flat amber field holds the head steady while the red spiral eye and open bared teeth create competing focal points; the warm ground keeps neither from dominating.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #274's blue field presses the face forward; nnxyz nnotb #267's amber ground holds the head at a slight distance, making the open mouth feel less frontal and more ambiguous.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #267

stops.whyHere: An open jaw and hollow eye sockets read as distress, but the acid-yellow ground and overlapping translucent circles push against that reading with something almost festive.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #267's amber is warm but neutral; nnxyz nnotb #287's yellow ground and bubble pattern create a direct visual argument with the skeletal jaw form above it.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #287

stops.whyHere: A flat bright blue field holds a face where heart and flower shapes stand in for eyes; the bared alternating teeth below sit in odd company with those softer eye forms.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #287's ground fights its subject; nnxyz nnotb #173's blue field is calm enough that the contrast between the flower-eye and the tooth row reads as a quieter, stranger tension.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #173

stops.whyHere: Saturated yellow pushes the central form forward; two red heart eye zones and a raw tooth row below create a compressed, contradictory surface on an advancing ground.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #173's blue holds the face at a distance; nnxyz nnotb #181's yellow advances it, making the same heart-eye and tooth-row combination feel louder and more insistent.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #181

stops.whyHere: Dense black loops over ochre and teal washes build a rounded head; the red-edged mouth bares a tight, narrow tooth row rather than a wide-open jaw, the mouth present but not gaping.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #181's yellow field is flat and advancing; nnxyz nnotb #201's layered ochre and teal washes give the ground depth, and the mouth closes slightly — teeth visible but contained.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #201

stops.whyHere: A teal-green field surrounds a heavy circular form; warm reds and oranges inside contrast with the cool ground, and the spiked jaw with white zigzag verticals reads differently against that temperature shift.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #201's ochre washes are warm throughout; nnxyz nnotb #207 splits warm interior from cool exterior, so the jaw and tooth marks read as heat pressing against a cooler surround.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #207

chapters.title: Two Faces, One Field
chapters.introduction: Four works where a second face, eye, or mouth form shares the composition — the tooth row doubled or placed alongside another presence within the same picture boundary.

stops.whyHere: Two face-like forms share a black field without merging: a ringed eye on the left, an open-mouthed form with visible teeth on the right — the gap between them as legible as either form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #207's single circular form sits alone in its field; nnxyz nnotb #135 places two distinct face-like structures side by side, making the space between them a third element.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #135

stops.whyHere: Two tooth-lined shapes appear within a single white-outlined oval, separated by a bold red-orange bar; the doubling is compressed inside one boundary rather than spread across the field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #135's two forms are spatially separate; nnxyz nnotb #270 folds two tooth rows inside one outline, so the doubling is harder to resolve into distinct voices.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #270

stops.whyHere: A tilted head holds two yellow circular eye forms and several rows of teeth; the multiplication of tooth rows across warm color bands makes a single expression impossible to isolate.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #270's doubled teeth sit inside a flat purple field; nnxyz nnotb #300 tilts the whole head and adds warm color bands, so the crowded tooth rows feel kinetic rather than static.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #300

stops.whyHere: A circular form under pressure from lines pulling outward in every direction; the open lower section packed with white verticals reads as a shout caught mid-release.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #300's tilted head is dense but contained; nnxyz nnotb #210 breaks the containing form open, with lines escaping outward and the tooth-like verticals exposed inside a dark cavity.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #210

chapters.title: Layered Marks and the Unresolved Face
chapters.introduction: Four works where accumulated marks, scribbled lines, and color patches build up across the surface so densely that the mouth is the last feature to become readable, if it does at all.

stops.whyHere: A grinning yellow disc crossed by bars edged with teeth; the smile sits below crossed marks and above a heavy red field, making the grin and the threat coexist on the same surface.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #210's form is circular and under outward pressure; nnxyz nnotb #262 is also a disc, but the pressure comes from crossed bars and a heavy red field pressing inward from below.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #262

stops.whyHere: A swollen olive-green face fills the frame completely; crossed scribbles in acid yellow and cyan sit over the bulk without softening it, and the bared teeth read as confrontational rather than joyful.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #262's disc floats within its field; nnxyz nnotb #172's face fills the frame to every edge, removing any breathing room between the bared teeth and the viewer.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #172

stops.whyHere: Two mismatched eyes — one gridded in yellow and black, one marked with a red X — give the face an off-balance stare; drips from above and the open-toothed mouth below pull the eye in opposite directions.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #172's surface is dense but the face reads as symmetrical; nnxyz nnotb #236 introduces deliberate asymmetry between the two eye zones, so the face reads as unstable rather than merely loud.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #236

stops.whyHere: Dark layered color pools inside the form while bright scattered lines fly outward; the bared tooth row and goggle shapes read as raw alarm against a black field that offers no softening context.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #236's gray ground gives the face some neutral space; nnxyz nnotb #160's black field removes it entirely, making the contrast between the dark core and the escaping bright lines feel abrupt.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #160
